newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hit by surging Nikkei.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hit by surging Nikkei.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures remained weak in late Tuesday trade after substantial gains in Tokyo stocks stoked fears of a rate hike in Japan.
"The Nikkei is considered a leading indicator and when it goes up like this, people start thinking Japan might raise rates," a broker with an Asian institution said.
He said large-lot sales pushed JGB futures through key technical support levels, causing the June contract to fall to a low of 124.30. It ended at 124.44 against a previous 125.46.

The sell-off in JGB futures dragged down Euroyen futures with December falling to a low of 98.92 early in the day. It stood at 98.94 at 1130 GMT against an IMM close at 99.00 on active volume of 24,715 lots.
The Nikkei share average ended up 666.17 points to 20,180.92 in Tokyo.
"People are pricing in a rate hike but most analysts still don't expect it till the first or second quarter of 1998," the trader said.
He said December Euroyen could edge up slightly to 99.00/01 before heading lower to 98.81.

A dealer with a European futures house said the JGB fall was triggered in part by talk of a large Tokyo corporate bond issue of 300 billion yen and a JGB auction later in the week, sparking concerns about excess supply.

Dealers said there was growing talk of investors switching from JGB futures to Nikkei futures, given the Nikkei stock market's bullish performance in recent weeks and growing concerns about a Japanese rate hike.
Eurodollar futures ended easier ahead of the U.S. Treasury Department's quarterly refunding auctions, featuring sales of three- and 10-year notes on Tuesday and Wednesday respectively.
December Eurodollars finished at 93.665 against their IMM close at 93.680.
